means: How much of the scene in front of and behind the focus point stays sharp. Shallow means a thin slice is sharp and everything else dissolves; deep means all of it is sharp.
does: Blurs the background and lifts the subject off it - the fastest character-from-background separation there is, and the knob that decides whether your world is a place or a texture. It is a real danbooru tag and it lands. But the model has TWO states, not a dial: deep focus, and blurry background. The card review says so and the measurement agrees - medium against shallow was that card's closest pair at 34.32, and split_diopter has essentially no representation and returns ordinary deep focus. It also behaves as GRAMMAR: writing depth of field declares the background is blurred, so a sharp background or scenery detail tag elsewhere in the same prompt cancels it, and you get neither.
reach_for_it: when the background is doing nothing for you and you want it gone, or on a close-up where the subject must be the only fact in the frame
